Answers below.

**h01** — S3 presign runner — every 12 hours — wired in `server/server.go:162-171`
- Component: `s3presign.Runner` (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:16`), which re-presigns S3 attachment URLs (`CheckAndPresign`, `runner.go:47`) so stored `reference` URLs don't expire; skips items presigned within the last 4 days (5‑day expiry) (`runner.go:85-91`).
- Schedule: `runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12` ticker (`runner.go:27,29-41`).
- Wiring: `Server.startBackgroundRunners` — `NewRunner` + immediate `RunOnce` at `server/server.go:162-163`, continuous `Run` goroutine at `server/server.go:166-171`; called from `Server.Start` (`server/server.go:129`).

**h02** — delivery function: `webhook.Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:120` (actual HTTP execution `safeClient.Do(req)` at `internal/webhook/webhook.go:152`; async path enqueues via `PostAsync` `webhook.go:184` drained by 4 goroutines started in `init()` `webhook.go:42-55`); protection: SSRF guard at dial time — `safeDialContext` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:59-77`) wired into the shared client's Transport (`webhook.go:32-37`), rejecting reserved/private IPs via `isReservedIP` against `reservedCIDRs` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:14-54`) — this also defeats DNS rebinding. Additional up-front check at config time: `webhook.ValidateURL` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:62`), called from `server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go:74,161,182`. Escape hatch: `webhook.AllowPrivateIPs` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:41`).

**h03** — abstraction package: `internal/idp` (`internal/idp/idp.go:1-8`, defines `IdentityProviderUserInfo`); implementation package: `internal/idp/oauth2` (`internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go:19-46`, `IdentityProvider` + `NewIdentityProvider`). Only OAuth2 ships; used at `server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go:121`.

**h04** — no; `mysql.NewDB` is referenced exactly once in the whole repo, inside the factory `NewDBDriver` (`store/db/db.go:22`). Full grep of `NewDB(` shows only `store/db/db.go:20,22,24` plus test-only sqlite uses (`store/deployment_config_test.go:416`, `store/demo_seed_test.go:24`) and the three declarations (`store/db/sqlite/sqlite.go:24`, `store/db/mysql/mysql.go:20`, `store/db/postgres/postgres.go:21`). The other `mysql` hits in `store/test/containers.go:101` are the testcontainers module and the `go-sql-driver/mysql` DSN parser, not the memos driver.

**h05** — mechanism: explicit Go code inside the delete-user transaction (no DB-level cascade for reactions).
- Two explicit deletes per driver: by memo content id and by creator — `store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:95,101` (impls at `:390`, `:402`), `store/db/postgres/user_delete.go:96,102` (impls at `:380`, `:400`), `store/db/mysql/user_delete.go:96,102` (impls at `:417`, `:437`).
- Evidence there is no database rule: the `reaction` table has no FK/`ON DELETE` clause in any dialect (`store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:92-99`, `store/migration/postgres/LATEST.sql:91-98`, `store/migration/mysql/LATEST.sql:91-98`); the only `ON DELETE CASCADE` in the schema is on `memo_share.memo_id` (`store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:109` and dialect equivalents).
- Entry point: `store.DeleteUser` (`store/user.go:171`) → `driver.DeleteUser` → `deleteUserTargetsTx`.

**r01** — Premise is wrong: there is no Redis anywhere in the repo (no client dependency, no config). The cache is a process-local in-memory cache: `store/cache/cache.go` (`Cache` struct `:66`, `sync.Map` + TTL sweeper). Three instances are created in `store.New` — `instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache` (`store/store.go:51-53`) — all with `DefaultTTL: 10 * time.Minute`, `CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute`, `MaxItems: 1000` (`store/store.go:40-45`; same defaults in `cache.DefaultConfig()` `store/cache/cache.go:57-63`). So user entries expire 10 minutes after being set (`store/user.go:141-143,147-168`); they are also refreshed on update (`store/user.go:126-133`) and invalidated on delete (`store/user_delete.go:39`).

**r02** — Premise is wrong: there is no rate-limiting middleware in the codebase. The only Echo middleware registered is `middleware.Recover()` and the CORS middleware (`server/server.go:51-52`); Connect/gRPC interceptors at `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:133` are auth/logging, not rate limiting. No `golang.org/x/time/rate`, no limiter dependency in `go.mod`; the only "rate limit" string in the repo is an aspirational comment about email sending (`internal/email/doc.go:86`). Related size guards that do exist: request body cap `maxAPIRequestBytes` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:141,144`) and concurrency semaphores for thumbnails/image processing (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:59-60`, `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:116`).

**r03** — Premise is wrong: there is no cron scheduler running and no nightly database-cleanup job. `internal/scheduler` exists as a cron-expression library (`internal/scheduler/scheduler.go`, `parser.go`), but it is imported only by its own tests/docs (`internal/scheduler/example_test.go:10`, `internal/scheduler/integration_test.go:13`) — it is never wired into the server. The only background work started at runtime is the 12-hour S3 presign ticker (`server/server.go:162-171`, `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27`), which refreshes presigned URLs, not database cleanup.

**r04** — Premise is wrong: neither. There is no message broker at all — no NATS, RabbitMQ/AMQP, or Kafka dependency or code in the repo, and no queue declaration. Webhook delivery is entirely in-process: a buffered Go channel `asyncPostQueue` of capacity 128 (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:39`) drained by 4 goroutines started in `init()` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:42-55`), fed by `webhook.PostAsync` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:184-196`, which drops the event when the buffer is full) and delivered by `webhook.Post` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:120`). Deliveries are lost on restart; there is no retry.

**r05** — Premise is wrong: there is no GraphQL schema or GraphQL server anywhere (no `graphql` reference in Go, TS, `go.mod`, or `package.json`). The public API is Protobuf-defined RPC exposed three ways: Connect-RPC over `/memos.api.v1.*` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:139-144`), gRPC-Gateway REST (`APIV1Service.RegisterGateway`, `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:65`), and MCP (`server/router/mcp`). Schemas live in `proto/api/v1/*.proto` (`memo_service.proto`, `user_service.proto`, `auth_service.proto`, `attachment_service.proto`, `idp_service.proto`, `instance_service.proto`, `shortcut_service.proto`, `ai_service.proto`, `common.proto`) with generated code in `proto/gen/api/v1`. Non-RPC HTTP surfaces: `/file/*` (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:121-125`), RSS (`server/router/rss/rss.go`), and `/healthz` (`server/server.go:67`).
